question: What does French-, German-, Chinese-, Japanese- and Korean-language work (papers, theses, proceedings, blogs, re-implementations, community discussion) add to the grokking picture as of October 2026, for algorithmic grokking: mechanisms, the finite-set recipe, acceleration (Grokfast, StableMax / softmax collapse, weight decay, schedules) and failure modes?
scope: Non-English sources only; the English core literature is handled separately (audit session lit notes, issue #259). Focus 2024 to Oct 2026; older only if foundational in that language community.
decision: Which grokking recipe and fixes ReLSM should adopt before its first finite-set grokking run (#249, #214), and which failure modes to guard against.
assumptions: English arXiv papers by Chinese-, Japanese- or Korean-speaking authors count only when native-language discussion adds something (replication, critique, detail).
Search: SearXNG (once Docker is up) plus built-in web search and direct site fetches.
gaps: No exact-recipe replication with embedding exemption, 32k tied vocab or final RMSNorm
Thin peer-reviewed native-language coverage in all five lanes
Zhihu/CSDN URLs fail automated citation checks (bot protection); read via browser pane
English delta lane read mostly at abstract level; 5 of its decision-relevant claims re-checked in synthesis
